ai.description: Jayaram's Bushfrog is a small, 20–25 mm frog. It features a brownish-grey dorsum with dark mottling and a distinct white spot on the snout. Its limbs possess prominent dark cross-bands.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes jayarami* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow-orange webbing between the toes, which is absent in most other sympatric bushfrogs.
ai.habitat: Raorchestes jayarami inhabits the high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Jayaram's Bushfrog is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights actively foraging for small insects among the foliage of its high-altitude forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes jayarami* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in leaf axils or vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: Raorchestes jayarami is endemic to the Western Ghats of Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes jayarami* consists of a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude shola forests.
